body:
THE NARROWS BOARD // NEW BLOOD / OLD SCARS SUBFORUM
Thread: What I Did With My First Payout
Started by: user PELLUCID_VOSS
Date: 14 Harvest 2199
Archived replies: 19 shown (47 total, remainder pruned for length)

---

**PELLUCID_VOSS** | C-tier | 14 Harvest

Saw a thread like this on the Eastgate board years ago and it helped me more than any guide did. So. What did you spend your first real payout on? Not the Φ80 you got for running a package to Sublevel 9. I mean the first time you looked at your account and thought: okay. Something changed. Go.

---

**TANITH_RYE** | C-tier (pending B review) | 14 Harvest

Gear. Obviously gear. But I'll be specific because vague answers are useless.

Φ340 came in from a three-person extraction job — I was the third person, did the least, got the least, fine. Spent Φ190 of it at Mira's on Concourse 7. Don't buy new. Mira pulls from ACS seizure lots and the markup is sane. Got a full-seal respirator (not a half-mask, a FULL seal — you want to work the lower Shelf, you need this, the particulate count down there will quietly kill you over eighteen months), a second-hand shockstick that needed recalibration but Mira did it while I waited, and a chest rig that fits over my existing jacket without screaming 'I have a chest rig.' Spent another Φ40 on six weeks of prepaid locker access at the Thirteenth Street depot so I have somewhere to stage out of that isn't my apartment.

Φ110 left. Put it in the account and did not touch it.

The respirator has already saved me twice. The shockstick once. The locker every single job.

---

**ORSOLYA** | B-tier | 14 Harvest

Rating Tanith: **EXACTLY RIGHT.**

The full-seal respirator note especially. Half the C-tier deaths I've seen in four years weren't dramatic. They were slow. Lungs, mostly. Or an infected cut because they were doing field work without sealed gloves. Gear that keeps you alive over time is worth more than gear that helps you fight.

Continue.

---

**MACE_ILLO** | C-tier | 15 Harvest

Paid off a debt.

Φ600 job, courier relay across three transit zones, I was moving something I didn't ask about which I now know was a bad call but I was new and I needed it. Φ600. First time I'd seen that number with my name on it.

I owed Φ510 to my uncle. Not a loan shark. My actual uncle, Benedek, who kept my mother and my two sisters fed for eight months after we came up from what used to be Kentucky. He never asked for it back. He said he never would. That's what made it worse.

I transferred it to him the same hour I got paid. He called me. He was angry. Said I needed that money. I said I needed to not owe it more. We didn't talk for a while after that.

I don't know if it was the right call financially. I know I slept differently after. I know I work differently when I'm not carrying that. So I don't regret it but I also don't know what it cost me in the long run. Maybe nothing. Maybe I'd have a better rig right now.

Benedek came to my B-review vouch ceremony. He brought food. We didn't talk about the money.

---

**ORSOLYA** | B-tier | 15 Harvest

Rating Mace: **SURVIVABLE CHOICE.**

Not wrong. Not right. Debt to family is a different kind of weight than debt to a broker and you can't always calculate it out. You're still here. Your uncle came to your vouch. That's something.

---

**FELIX_DRUCKER** | C-tier | 15 Harvest

Bought a BCI upgrade for my daughter.

She's nine. The school in our block has a shared terminal room, twelve terminals for four hundred kids, and the kids with basic BCIs get twice the instruction time because they can interface directly with the curriculum modules. She's been borrowing headsets. Borrowed headsets are disgusting and they don't calibrate right and she was falling behind.

Φ280 for a certified secondhand Nexus Junior, calibrated for her specifically, one year of update coverage. She put it in at the clinic on a Tuesday. By Thursday she was doing math two grades ahead of where she'd been.

I don't care what anyone says about that spend. I would do it every time.

---

**ORSOLYA** | B-tier | 15 Harvest

Rating Felix: **EXACTLY RIGHT.**

No notes. Good job.

---

**CASP_NOURI** | C-tier | 16 Harvest

Okay I'm going to be honest.

I spent Φ400 on a jacket.

Not a tactical jacket. Not an armored jacket. A jacket. It was real leather — or real-adjacent leather, the lab stuff — and it had an internal heating mesh and it looked incredible and I had been wearing the same three shirts for two years and I just. I bought the jacket.

I wore it to a job three days later and tore a panel on a fence wire and the repair cost Φ60 and I cried a little in the depot bathroom.

I still have the jacket. It still looks good. The patch is mostly invisible. I don't regret it but I do regret not getting the armored lining option which was only Φ55 more and I was already spending Φ400 on a JACKET so I don't know what I was thinking.

Don't buy the jacket. Or if you buy the jacket, get the armored lining.

---

**ORSOLYA** | B-tier | 16 Harvest

Rating Casp: **BAD CHOICE.**

But the funniest bad choice in the thread so far so partial credit. The armored lining note is genuinely useful. File that away, new people: if you're going to make a stupid purchase, at least make it functional.

---

**TANITH_RYE** | C-tier (pending B review) | 16 Harvest

Casp I saw you in that jacket at the Thirteenth Street depot last month and I thought you were a Canopy kid who got lost. That's not an insult. It's almost useful.

---

**CASP_NOURI** | C-tier | 16 Harvest

Yeah that's happened twice actually. Might be worth something.

---

**V_SABLE** | B-tier | 17 Harvest

Saved it. All of it. Φ520. Put it in a cold account — not linked to my BCI, not accessible from the grid, a physical card that lives in a sealed envelope in my locker at Thirteenth Street. (Hi Tanith.)

I know people think saving is a personality type and maybe it is but here's the actual math: every job has a gap between the job ending and the next job beginning. Sometimes it's two weeks. Twice it's been two months. You cannot negotiate well when you're hungry. You cannot turn down a bad job when you have nothing. That Φ520 is not wealth. It's margin. It's the difference between taking a job because I chose it and taking a job because I had no choice.

I have Φ1,100 in that account now. I have turned down four jobs in eighteen months. Three of them went bad. One of the freelancers who took a job I turned down is dead.

Save the money.

---

**ORSOLYA** | B-tier | 17 Harvest

Rating Sable: **EXACTLY RIGHT.**

And yes she's smug about it. She's earned it.

---

**PELLUCID_VOSS** | C-tier | 17 Harvest

Sable what do you do when the gap is already two months and you have Φ0 in that account and a broker is offering Φ300 for something that smells wrong

---

**V_SABLE** | B-tier | 17 Harvest

You take the job and you be very careful and you start the account the moment you get paid. I said save it. I didn't say the first month is easy.

---

**USER: DOCKWHISTLE** | no tier listed | 18 Harvest

I'll tell you what I did with my first payout.

Φ900. Big job, C-tier shouldn't have been on it, I was the fourth body and two of the other three were B-tier solid. We came out with everything we went in for. I was twenty-two and I felt like I'd won something.

I bought rounds for everyone at the Lowline bar on Shelf 4 for three consecutive nights. I told anyone who would listen about the job. Details. Names. Routes. I was an idiot. I thought the Lowline was safe — it's freelancer-adjacent, everyone in there is connected somehow, what's the harm.

ACS raided the bar on the fourth night. Not for me specifically. But two of the people I'd talked to loudly were wanted on a surveillance flag and they'd been sitting next to me for hours and I was on the room's passive capture.

They held me for eleven days. They didn't have enough to charge me but they didn't need to charge me to hold me. Eleven days. They took my rig, my BCI access, my shoes. I came out with nothing and a note in whatever system they keep that I've never been able to fully verify or fully dispute.

I have no tier rating. I work Ghost-adjacent because I have to, not because I'm good enough for it. Every job I take is one where the broker already knows the problem with my record and has decided they don't care, which means they're usually jobs other people have declined.

I'm still here. I don't know if that's luck or stubbornness or just that I'm too boring to kill cleanly.

Don't talk about the job. Don't talk about the job. Don't talk about the job.

Not in a bar. Not to your friends. Not here, actually — Pellucid, this is a kiosk board, it's mostly okay, but be specific about what you share and with whom.

The jacket is a stupid buy. The jacket will not get you disappeared.

Know the difference.

---

**ORSOLYA** | B-tier | 18 Harvest

No rating for Dockwhistle.

Just: read that one twice.
